subject: Bank of Canada hikes to 2.5%, prime hits 4.70% today
bodyMarkdown:
If you carry a variable mortgage, a HELOC or a line of credit, your borrowing cost went up this morning. The Bank of Canada raised rates yesterday for the first time in more than three years, and the big banks pushed prime to 4.70 per cent effective today.

## What the Bank actually did

Governing Council raised its target for the overnight rate by 25 basis points to 2.5 per cent yesterday morning, with the Bank Rate at 2.75 per cent and the deposit rate at 2.45 per cent. TD Economics called it the first increase since July 2023, and MoneySense noted the rate had sat at 2.25 per cent since the October 2025 cut. Canadian Mortgage Trends reported on Wednesday that the six largest banks each moved prime up a quarter point to 4.70 per cent effective October 29, which is this morning. The **prime rate** is the posted number banks price variable loans off, so variable mortgages, home equity lines and most car and student lines reset with it. The Bank said it will decide one meeting at a time and that further increases may be needed.

## Why hike into a weak job market

This is the part I keep turning over. Statistics Canada reported on October 9 that employment fell by 68,000 in September, the second monthly drop in a row, and that unemployment rose to 6.5 per cent. Young workers took most of it, down 48,000, with youth unemployment at 13 per cent. That is not an economy you normally lean on. The Bank's own statement says there is still excess supply, meaning more idle workers and capacity than demand needs, and that **core inflation**, the measures that strip out the noisiest prices, sits close to 2 per cent. Oil did the deciding. Brent settled at US$115.32 a barrel on Wednesday and WTI at US$102.78 after Houthi attacks on Saudi Arabia's largest refinery, and CPI, near 3 per cent since April, is now expected to reach about 3.5 per cent by year end.

## The Fed went the other way

Washington looked at the same oil price and sat still. CNBC reported that the Fed held its target range at 3.75 to 4 per cent yesterday on a 10 to 2 vote, with Governor Lisa Cook and Cleveland Fed President Beth Hammack both wanting a quarter point increase. The statement described activity as "expanding at a strong pace" and said inflation remains elevated. So the Americans are more than a point above us and holding while we climb, which is the opposite of the gap most people were trading a year ago. The Bank put the Canadian dollar at about 71 cents US, back to the level it assumed in July. A soft loonie makes imported food and machinery dearer in Canadian dollars, which is its own slow drip of inflation. Oil gave some back this morning, with Brent off roughly 1.4 per cent to US$113.73 on diplomatic efforts over Iran, The National reported.

## The takeaway

If you are on a variable mortgage, open your statement today and work out whether the payment itself rose or whether the payment held flat while more of it went to interest, because those two are very different problems. If you renew within a year, stop treating a hold as the base case: Yahoo Finance Canada reported that RBC expects three more hikes in total while Desjardins expects none for the rest of 2026, and that spread is the real question. I am watching the October CPI release and the next jobs print. If unemployment keeps rising while oil slides back toward US$100, the Bank's own argument for moving again in December gets thinner.
